lines.text: T-minus three. Two. One. Ignition.
Liftoff. We have liftoff of Falcon 9.
Vehicle is supersonic.
Max Q. The vehicle is through the region of maximum aerodynamic pressure.
MECO. Main engine cutoff confirmed.
Stage separation confirmed.
Second engine start. M-Vac ignition is good.
Fairing separation confirmed. The payload is now exposed to space.
SECO. Second engine cutoff.
Nominal orbit insertion. Falcon 9 has delivered the payload to orbit.
Abort, abort, abort. Engines have been shut down.
Hold, hold, hold. We are standing down on today's launch attempt.
We have lost the vehicle. All controllers, lock your consoles.
First stage has started its flip maneuver.
Entry burn startup.
Entry burn shutdown. Grid fins are guiding the booster.
Landing legs deployed.
Landing burn startup.
The Falcon has landed! First stage is down on the droneship.
We've lost telemetry from the first stage. It looks like we did not stick the landing today.
Altitude ten kilometers.
Fifty kilometers altitude, everything looking good.
One hundred kilometers. Falcon 9 is now in space.
Altitude one hundred fifty kilometers.
Downrange distance, five hundred kilometers.
All stations, this is the launch director. Standing by for launch.
Weather is green, range is green. We are go for launch.
Propellant load is complete. Vehicle is ready for flight.
Stage one propulsion is nominal.
Vehicle remains on a nominal trajectory.
Guidance is nominal. The vehicle is pitching downrange.
Power and telemetry look good.
Stage two propulsion is nominal.
M-Vac is performing as expected.
Second stage guidance has converged.
We continue to track Falcon 9 through the ground stations.
Booster is on a ballistic trajectory toward the droneship.
Recovery team is standing by.
Grid fins are active. The booster is steering toward the landing zone.
The second stage is coasting in orbit.
Telemetry from the second stage remains strong.
That is a beautiful view of Earth from orbit.
